spot.html_text: Albo formulates a list of the fundamental beliefs of religion from within his theory of principles (which we will explain in the next section), since he considers similar lists composed by his predecessors to be insufficient. Instead of naming the principles of Mosaic law (“the Torah of Moses”) as, for example, Maimonides did in his well-known list of thirteen principles, Albo widens his target and lists the principles of “divine law,” in an effort to understand the principles of Judaism within
